reason: The text does not exemplify humility as a leadership model. Rather, it depicts Pharaoh repeatedly refusing to accept criticism and God's commands, demonstrating the opposite of humble leadership. When Pharaoh briefly acknowledges wrongdoing ('I have sinned'), his admission is coerced by plague and insincere, as evidenced by his immediate relapse into stubbornness afterward ('he hardened his heart again'). The passage emphasizes God's demonstration of power and judgment through successive plagues to force compliance, not the virtue of accepting criticism with humility. Moses, by contrast, delivers God's word obediently but is not presented as a model responding to criticism—his own doubts are addressed by divine reassurance, not through humility or accepting human criticism.
